findings.title: Nil dereference when `TopicUser` record does not exist
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user has never visited or interacted with the topic (for example, if they received the notification email via `mailing_list_mode`, were mentioned in a topic they haven't opened yet, or followed an unsubscribe link directly). Accessing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and return a 500 error. Also, mutating and saving `tu` directly bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, and publishes the change on `MessageBus`.

findings.title: GET request to `unsubscribe` mutates topic notification level without confirmation
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is wired to a `GET` route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and immediately modifies the user's `TopicUser#notification_level` in the database. Furthermore, because the Ember `TopicUnsubscribeRoute` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (which fetches `/t/:id.json`) rather than `/unsubscribe`, and the HTML response preloads `topic_#{id}` with the already-mutated state, automated email link scanners, browser prefetchers, or accidental refreshes will change the user's notification level on a `GET` request (and a second hit will drop a `regular` user down to `muted`).

findings.title: Client-side navigation to `/unsubscribe` does not actually unsubscribe
findings.body: `TopicUnsubscribeRoute#model` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which only fetches the topic view (`/t/:id.json` or preloaded data) and never hits `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`. It only works on a full-page load because the Rails `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action runs on the initial HTML request and preloads the topic JSON. If the route is entered via a client-side transition, or if the user must log in first and is redirected back within the Ember app, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is never called and the user's notification level is not changed, even though the template tells them they have stopped receiving notifications.
